topicName: Inference Optimization (Triton Inference Server, vLLM, TensorRT)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Production Deep Learning Inference Optimization: Triton, vLLM, and TensorRT"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Deploying deep learning models to production requires minimizing latency and maximizing throughput while controlling operational costs. This tutorial explores the industry standard toolchain for high-performance inference: NVIDIA TensorRT for model compilation, Triton Inference Server for multi-model serving, and vLLM for optimized Large Language Model (LLM) serving."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Accelerating Computer Vision and Standard Models with TensorRT"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"TensorRT is an SDK for high-performance deep learning inference. It includes a optimizer and runtime that load, calibrate, and generate optimized execution plans for deep learning models."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import tensorrt as trt

TRT_LOGGER = trt.Logger(trt.Logger.WARNING)
builder = trt.Builder(TRT_LOGGER)
network = builder.create_network(1 << int(trt.NetworkDefinitionCreationFlag.EXPLICIT_BATCH))
parser = trt.OnnxParser(network, TRT_LOGGER)

with open('model.onnx', 'rb') as model:
    parser.parse(model.read())

config = builder.create_builder_config()
config.set_memory_pool_limit(trt.MemoryPoolType.WORKSPACE, 1 << 30)
config.set_flag(trt.BuilderFlag.FP16)

serialized_engine = builder.build_serialized_network(network, config)
with open('model.plan', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(serialized_engine)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Serving Models at Scale using Triton Inference Server"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Triton Inference Server standardizes model deployment across cloud and edge, supporting multiple frameworks such as TensorRT, PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and TensorFlow. It enables concurrent execution and dynamic batching out of the box."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"name: "tensorrt_model"
platform: "tensorrt_plan"
max_batch_size: 64
input [
  {
    name: "input"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 3, 224, 224 ]
  }
]
output [
  {
    name: "output"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 1000 ]
  }
]
dynamic_batching { }
"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. High-Throughput LLM Serving with vLLM"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditional LLM serving suffers from severe memory waste due to key-value (KV) cache fragmentation. vLLM introduces PagedAttention, which manages KV cache memory in blocks, drastically increasing concurrency and throughput."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

prompts = [
    "Hello, my name is",
    "The future of AI is",
]
sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=100)

llm = LLM(model="facebook/opt-125m", tensor_parallel_size=1)
outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params)

for output in outputs:
    prompt = output.prompt
    generated_text = output.outputs[0].text
    print(f"Prompt: {prompt!r}, Generated text: {generated_text!r}")"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Production Deployment"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use FP16 or INT8 quantization via TensorRT or bitsandbytes to reduce memory bandwidth bottlenecks."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enable Triton's dynamic batching to group incoming requests and improve GPU utilization."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverage vLLM's continuous batching for LLM workloads to avoid idle time during autoregressive generation."}]
